      How to read this market

      Crypto looks like one asset class from a distance and like six from up close. Bitcoin trades like a macro asset: a scarce, non-sovereign store of value whose price responds to liquidity conditions and ETF flows. Layer-1 platforms are closer to technology equity: their tokens pay for computation and their value rests on whether applications and users show up. Stablecoins are the market's cash, and their supply is a better gauge of money entering or leaving than any price. DeFi tokens are the only category with auditable revenue. Memecoins are pure attention. Exchange tokens are something like equity in a venue, with the governance rights removed.

      These categories move together in a crash — correlations go to one when leverage unwinds — but they diverge sharply over a cycle. Bitcoin dominance rising means capital is defensive; falling means risk appetite is spreading down the list. That single ratio, charted on the dominance page, explains more of the market than any headline.

      The pages that follow take each sector in turn, with the same structure: what it is, who the main assets are, what the numbers say, and where the numbers lie. The how-to-evaluate page collects the metrics into a checklist, and the risks page lists the ways people have actually lost money, ranked by size.
